children: Largest hunger relief investment in Foundation history includes $1.2 million for Ohio as part of a $5 million regional initiative supporting 140 organizations

AKRON, Ohio, Sept. 1, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The FirstEnergy Foundation is making its largest investment in hunger relief to date, awarding $1.2 million to 29 Ohio food banks and pantries during Hunger Action Month. The grants are part of a $5 million initiative supporting 140 hunger relief organizations across six states and the District of Columbia, helping stock local shelves and keep meals on tables in households facing food insecurity.

The funding is expected to provide more than 3.6 million meals for families and neighbors across Ohio, helping food banks and pantries meet growing demand in communities served by Ohio Edison, The Illuminating Company and Toledo Edison.
Funding Organizations on the Front Lines of Hunger Relief

National Hunger Action Month, observed each September, raises awareness of food insecurity and encourages volunteerism, advocacy and charitable giving to help address hunger in local communities. Despite ongoing efforts by food banks and nonprofit organizations, food insecurity remains a significant challenge across the country and in Ohio.

Feeding America estimates that more than 1.8 million Ohioans, or 15.3% of the population, experienced food insecurity in 2024, including approximately 535,000 children. Across the state, food banks and pantries continue to play a critical role in helping families access nutritious meals as they navigate ongoing economic pressures.
Torrence L. Hinton, President, FirstEnergy Ohio:

"No one should have to wonder where their next meal is coming from. Across Ohio, food banks and pantries are working every day to meet growing needs, but they can't do it alone. This investment will help provide more than 3.6 million meals for families, seniors and children while strengthening the organizations on the front lines of hunger relief. We're proud to support their work and to stand beside them through volunteer service in the communities we call home."
Michelle M. Brown, CEO & President, Children's Hunger Alliance (CHA):

"We are thrilled to grow our collaboration with the FirstEnergy Foundation to help children reach their full potential, providing nutritious meals and food education right where they are, every day of the year. Their investment will do more than expand programs — it will drive meaningful, lasting change in childhood nutrition across Northeast Ohio. Together, we can ensure that children have the nourishment they need not only to succeed in school, but to thrive in life. The FirstEnergy Foundation is helping power the solution. CHA is ready to deliver it."
Supporting 29 Hunger Relief Organizations Across Ohio

Building on last year's initiative, the Foundation expanded its Ohio support to 29 organizations in 2026, including 16 first-time recipients, and increased investments in several of the state's food banks and pantries. Employee Volunteers Help Food Banks Stretch Resources

In addition to financial support, FirstEnergy employees regularly volunteer with food banks, pantries and other nonprofit organizations across Ohio. Through the company's Volunteer Time Off (VTO) program, employees can provide hands-on support that helps organizations serve more families while reducing operating costs.

In 2025, employees contributed approximately 28,500 volunteer hours across FirstEnergy's service territory, including thousands of hours supporting hunger relief organizations. Based on the 2025 national value of a volunteer hour of $36.14, those efforts represent more than $1 million in additional community support.

The FirstEnergy Foundation supports 501(c)(3) organizations across FirstEnergy's operational area, helping them build capacity, strengthen outcomes and deliver lasting impact. Giving priorities include housing stability, hunger relief, workforce development and STEM initiatives that reflect community needs and the company's strategic focus. Combined with the Hunger Action Month grants, the Foundation has distributed nearly $6.5 million in community support across FirstEnergy's operational area to date in 2026.
